title: Recipes from the River: Oklahoma Onion Burgers
contentHtml:
Quick, easy, oniony smash burgers: How a Depression-era burger hack became one of America's most beloved flavor profiles.

For the third and final night of our trip to the Moab Music Festival, it was burger night. You'll get a look at how these came together in tomorrow's episode of Cooking on the River—keep your eyes peeled for the series finale!

The theme of this event was This Land: Exploring how quintessentially American music and food grew from global exchange and innovation, and these Oklahoma Onion Burger are no exception. Their origins trace back to Great Depression–era diners in El Reno, Oklahoma, where cooks would stretch beef with inexpensive onions. This workaround has since become a beloved technique in its own right that's more popular today than ever.

At our camp, we served these alongside our Red Cabbage & Dill Slaw and an impromptu version of this Japanese Potato Salad—using only the excess ingredients we had lying around—if you're looking to recreate the experience at home.

Every recipe I publish here is personally tested, tasted, and approved.

Serves: 4 double burgers

Ingredients

  • 1 ½ pounds 80/20 ground beef

  • 1 large yellow onion, very thinly sliced

  • 8 slices American cheese

  • 4 soft hamburger buns

  • Kosher salt

  • Freshly ground black pepper

  • Sliced dill pickles, for serving

  • Yellow mustard or other condiments, optional

Method

  1. Portion the patties. Divide beef into eight 3-ounce portions. Massage each portion briefly until cohesive and tacky, then roll into a smooth ball. Refrigerate until ready to cook.

  2. Prepare the patties. Press each ball into a disk about 3 inches wide. Season with salt and pepper. Flip and mound each patty generously with sliced onions. Do not season the onions yet.

  3. Smash. Heat a cast-iron skillet, carbon-steel skillet, or griddle over high heat until very hot. Place patties onion-side up on the dry cooking surface. Using a stiff spatula, smash through the onions and beef to form very thin patties, concentrating on getting the edges especially thin. Season onions lightly with salt and pepper.

  4. Sear. Cook without moving until the beef edges are deeply browned and crisp, 1 to 2 minutes. Scrape thoroughly underneath each patty to preserve the crust, then flip onion-side down, tucking stray onions underneath.

  5. Steam. Top each patty with American cheese. Stack the patties in pairs to make four doubles. Place bun tops over each double, then place bun bottoms split-side down on top. Cover and cook until onions are browned, cheese is melted, and buns are steamed, 1 to 2 minutes.

  6. Serve. Remove bun bottoms. Add pickles and condiments as desired. Transfer each double burger onto its bottom bun and serve immediately.
